source_description: Native instruction bytes from the read-only Exanima 0.9.5.2g Steam build 25803178 research archive; controlled-head sampler identity separately confirmed in an authorized live session.
scope: Reviewed member instruction windows and binding-table references. These checks do not prove every caller, object lifetime, anatomical label, physical rule or callee implementation.

fields.provenance: RBX is the behaviour argument. RSI is loaded from behaviour+28 at 0xBFA7D; this load then reads character+18. The result is a scene node because the next load obtains its +130 sector and +64 sector origin for aim-coordinate conversion.
fields.name: character::sceneNode

fields.provenance: RAX reloads the saved incoming character from stack+E0, corresponding to local_108 in the decompile. This byte at character+4C8 gates pose interpolation together with the same character's +9B8 motion; it is not a part pointer or animation-record displacement.
fields.name: character::physicsLive

fields.provenance: RAX is loaded from behaviour local_10+28. Native player processing tests the character's DWORD weapon count before copying gaze into unarmed facing/movement-facing. GripSelect independently checks character+920 before dereferencing its +928 weapon slot.
fields.name: character::weaponCount

fields.provenance: RBX preserves the incoming character argument. After testing DWORD character+920, native grip selection loads character+928 into RSI and inspects the item's +18 scene node and attributes. The same function reads [character+index*8+928] at 0x15226D; heldItemRelease compares and compacts these pointer slots. The cursorAim +928 float candidate was rejected because its base is behaviour, not character.
fields.name: character::weapons

fields.provenance: RBX is behaviour local_10[5], the character, in this native player-dispatch branch. Native code tests its +988 pointer, then uses that object's +6E0 weapon-data pointer when non-null. This is separate from the +928 equipped-weapon array.
fields.name: character::swingWeapon

fields.provenance: RBX is the character from behaviour+28. The DWORD at character+9B8 is compared against motion 0x2D while the same branch classifies combat button presses; this same root field is compared to other motion IDs throughout the native dispatcher.
fields.name: character::motion

fields.provenance: RBX is the character loaded from behaviour+28. CVTSS2SD reads a 32-bit float at character+A28 after the character's state/swing-bit tests; native code compares it with a timing threshold for the active motion.
fields.name: character::motionProgress

fields.provenance: RBX is the character from behaviour local_10[5]. This LEA passes character+A30 as the destination to native vector construction 0x19390 before world queries. Width 8 is the encoded address operand only; this instruction does not itself establish a vector data span.
fields.name: character::travelTarget

fields.provenance: RDX is the character from behaviour local_10[5]. Native code copies its gaze at +CB0/+CB8 into +A48/+A50. This selected store writes eight bytes; the following four-byte store supplies the third vector component, independently establishing a 12-byte logical vector.
fields.name: character::movementFacing

fields.provenance: RDX is loaded from behaviour local_10[5], the character. Native player processing copies character+AB4 as a qword and character+ABC as a dword into position globals. This instruction witnesses an eight-byte read within the native 12-byte vector, not an eight-byte vector type.
fields.name: character::position

fields.provenance: RBX is the character from behaviour+28. MOVSS reads its +AD4 float and subtracts it from behaviour+1B0 aim heading; native grip-dependent angular thresholds then classify the combat press.
fields.name: character::bodyHeading

fields.provenance: BEAC0 loads RSI from behaviour+28 at 0xBEB2D. LEA RDX,[RSI+CB0] addresses the character gaze vector for native opponent scoring. Subsequent MULSS instructions read floats at RDX+0, +4 and +8, establishing the 12-byte extent. LEA has an eight-byte address operand, not an eight-byte data load. This supersedes the C280A copy witness so activation verifies the exact scoring consumer adapted by input11.
fields.name: character::gaze

fields.provenance: RAX is the character from behaviour local_10[5]. MOVSS reads the +CBC scalar and compares it against a native distance threshold before setting behaviour hover-state bits.
fields.name: character::gazeDistance

fields.provenance: RDX is the character from behaviour local_10[5]. Native player processing copies +CC0 as a qword and +CC8 as a dword to its adjacent saved-aim vector. This witnesses the start of a 12-byte vector while the actual selected read is eight bytes.
fields.name: character::aimDirection

fields.provenance: RDX is the character from behaviour local_10[5]. Native code copies character+CB0/+CB8 gaze into +CFC/+D04. This instruction is the first eight-byte destination store; the following dword store establishes the 12-byte vector extent.
fields.name: character::facing

fields.provenance: The immediately preceding RIP-relative load at 0x11F293 fetches EXP_controlled_dynamics_slot, the controlled character. Character+D40 then yields its behaviour, whose +928 filter scalar is adjusted in this branch; the same root+D40 pointer is passed to native cursor-aim update 0xBF630 elsewhere in this body.
fields.name: character::behaviour

fields.provenance: RBX preserves the incoming character, whose state flags, motion progress and grip fields are used earlier in this body. Character+D48 yields the torso-reference physical part; its +550 transform converts the selected hand point, and the adjacent load of the same part's +2A0 transform converts the swing-weapon origin. This is a required character-layout witness even though its owner also implements defense.
fields.name: character::chestPart

fields.provenance: At 0xC1D33 RBX is loaded from the behaviour argument+28; this next instruction reads the character's +DF4 DWORD and dispatches native character states. The owning pointer is established immediately before the witness.
fields.name: character::stateFlags

fields.provenance: RAX is first reloaded from the saved behaviour argument and then from behaviour+28. The native dispatcher reads character+DF8 as a DWORD and tests bit 0x100 before allowing live-player input processing.
fields.name: character::lifeFlags

fields.provenance: The explore function's argument is behaviour; RAX is loaded from its +28 character link. This qword store clears character+E50 after the ordinary-exploration state check, before movement and aim handling.
fields.name: character::contextualTarget

fields.provenance: RBX is the incoming character and R8 is the hand index. The same character was just written into the incoming physical item's +580 backlink at 0x155C3C. This load indexes character+E78 by eight-byte pointer entries to obtain the selected hand part, paired with the subsequent +E88 held-item store.
fields.name: character::handParts

fields.provenance: RBX is the incoming character; R12 preserves the incoming attached physical item; R8 is the hand index. This store writes that item into character+E88 indexed by eight bytes, paired with the item+580 character backlink and character+E78 selected hand. HeldItemRelease clears these same hand-indexed slots.
fields.name: character::heldItems

fields.provenance: RCX remains the character argument throughout native cleanup, which first walks its +920/+928 weapon array and +E78 hands. This DWORD comparison reads character+F5C, then the native cleanup writes -1 when nonnegative. DefenseAttackUpdate independently compares character+F5C against the targeted character's +9B8 motion.
fields.name: character::defenseIncomingMotion

fields.provenance: RCX is the character argument, already established by its weapon and hand fields in the same native body. Native cleanup tests byte character+12F3 here, clears it at 0x162F59, and can then call native posture cleanup. This byte belongs to native defense state.
fields.name: character::defenseActive

fields.provenance: RDX is the character from behaviour local_10[5]. This four-byte store writes a native float constant to character+100C when keyWord bit 0x10 is set; adjacent COMISS reads of the same field establish scalar floating-point use.
fields.name: character::duckAmount

fields.provenance: RBX is the character from behaviour+28. Native player dispatch reads its +1018 DWORD while character state is 2 and tests the 0x300000 mask before checking motion progress.
fields.name: character::swingBits

fields.provenance: RBX is the character from behaviour+28. This DWORD comparison at +1068 selects native angular thresholds for combat press classification. GripSelect independently assigns the same character field from held-weapon attributes and resolves its +1070 grip entry.
fields.name: character::gripFlags

fields.provenance: RBX is the character argument. Immediately after calling native grip lookup 0x155250 with this character's +1068 grip flags, the return pointer in RAX is stored at character+1070. HeldItemRelease also restores this exact pointer field to the default grip entry.
fields.name: character::gripEntry

fields.provenance: RDX is the character from behaviour local_10[5]. CVTSS2SD reads float character+10B8; the next scalar read takes character+10BC, which is multiplied by a threshold and compared with this current balance.
fields.name: character::balance

fields.provenance: RDX remains the character from behaviour local_10[5]. CVTSS2SD reads float character+10BC directly after current balance +10B8, then native code scales it for the balance threshold comparison.
fields.name: character::balanceMax

fields.provenance: RDX is the character loaded through behaviour local_10[5]. Native input processing ORs bit 8 into its +10F4 DWORD while processing the native run-key bit and character movement state; other branches update that same gait flags word.
fields.name: character::gaitFlags

fields.provenance: The behaviour argument+28 yields the current character; its +E38 yields the targeted character. At 0xAE422 RAX loads that target, and this instruction reads target-character+11E0, then uses the result as a physical part via +280 position, +294 extent and +2AC pose axis. The same target is traversed through its +9E0 body-part list in this body. This witnesses the character-class part slot on the target character, not a direct read of the controlled character's slot; the head label follows the existing anatomy mapping.
fields.name: character::headPart

fields.provenance: RAX is the character loaded from behaviour local_10[5]. Native dispatcher tests byte character+12EA in its ordinary-movement branch before deciding which behaviour movement state to clear or retain.
fields.name: character::walking

fields.provenance: RBX is the character from behaviour+28. The native dispatcher tests qword character+1230 for null and then calls through that same offset at 0xC1F27, proving a function-pointer-sized callback field.
fields.name: character::actionCallback

fields.provenance: RAX is the character from behaviour local_10[5]. Its +12FE byte selects exploration versus combat input branches, which call the native explore and combat-step routines on the original behaviour.
fields.name: character::combatStance

fields.provenance: RAX reloads the incoming behaviour argument. Its +28 qword is placed in RBX and immediately used as the owner of +DF4 state flags, followed by the character movement, motion and combat fields throughout native player dispatch.
fields.name: behaviour::character

fields.provenance: RAX is the saved incoming behaviour, local_10. The native dispatcher clears DWORD behaviour+30 before rebuilding its hover/distance bits from the linked character and current aim state.
fields.name: behaviour::hoverState

fields.provenance: RAX reloads the saved behaviour argument from the local stack slot, without following +28. This byte at behaviour+58 gates the native player-input path after separate linked-character life-state checks.
fields.name: behaviour::inactive

fields.provenance: RAX is the saved behaviour argument. Native input dispatch clears DWORD behaviour+90 in the combat press-state reset path; this is distinct from the global binding table's interact offset +90.
fields.name: behaviour::swingState

fields.provenance: RAX is the saved behaviour argument. MOVSS reads float behaviour+1B0, then subtracts the linked character's body heading +AD4 before native left/right combat press classification.
fields.name: behaviour::aimHeading

fields.provenance: RCX reloads local_10, the original behaviour argument, at this function's final result publication. The output point is copied to behaviour+854 as a qword and +85C as a dword; this witness is the eight-byte part of a separately visible 12-byte point copy.
fields.name: behaviour::aimPoint

fields.provenance: RAX is the saved behaviour argument, not its linked character. Native player dispatch clears DWORD behaviour+890 before rebuilding the native attack-press classification bits.
fields.name: behaviour::pressFlags

fields.provenance: RDX is the saved behaviour argument. Native code compares qword behaviour+898 with GUI manager+48 captured view; a different non-null capture suppresses gameplay input. AimPoint independently uses behaviour+898 as the viewport for projection.
fields.name: behaviour::view

fields.provenance: RDX is the saved incoming behaviour argument. Native combat-step processing writes the current movement state from behaviour+198 into behaviour+8F8 under its linked character's movement-state condition, then compares and timestamps subsequent pending movement changes.
fields.name: behaviour::pendingMove

fields.provenance: RAX is the saved behaviour argument. Native combat press classification reads DWORD behaviour+8E4 and compares elapsed native time against 0x12C while deciding whether successive attack presses form a sequence.
fields.name: behaviour::lastPressTime

fields.provenance: RBX preserves the behaviour argument. LEA behaviour+90C passes its embedded aim filter to native filter/turn routine 0xBF260; the same address is passed to native filter push 0xBF1C0 and update 0xBF380 later in this body. Width 8 denotes the encoded address operand, not the filter's complete data size.
fields.name: behaviour::aimFilter

fields.provenance: RBX preserves the behaviour argument. Native exploration writes byte behaviour+96C when native analog movement exceeds its epsilon and gameplay owns the relevant view, then tests the same byte before constructing movement input.
fields.name: behaviour::moveIntent

fields.provenance: This function's incoming GUI controller is not the field owner. At 0x121CC3 RAX loads EXP_controlled_dynamics_slot; at 0x121CCA it follows character+D40 to behaviour. This byte comparison then reads behaviour+96F while deciding interaction release, together with the configured interaction key and drag-manager flags.
fields.name: behaviour::interactionLatch

fields.provenance: RAX reloads the saved behaviour argument. Native combat press handling tests byte behaviour+96E before classifying ordinary LMB input. InteractionPoll independently writes this same byte through controlled-character+D40 when native interaction retains or releases input.
fields.name: behaviour::pressBlocked

fields.provenance: R12 is the current physical part: at 0x17691C-0x176926 it is loaded from the actor's +918 part-pointer array with the sign-extended part index. This DWORD read is immediately masked with 0x4000 at 0x176BE4, gating the extra-rotation quaternion consumer at 0x176BF5-0x176BFD. Other +C candidates on behaviour/view objects were excluded.
fields.name: bodyPart::flags

fields.provenance: R12 preserves incoming RDX (the attached physical part), whose +580 is explicitly assigned the incoming actor earlier in this function. Its +18 pointer becomes RSI. The subsequent code writes RSI+94/+9C, builds scene-node transform RSI+40, and uses that transform to reconstruct this same part's tetrahedron at R12+F0/+FC/+108/+114.
fields.name: bodyPart::meshNode

fields.provenance: RBX is the incoming physical part, copied from RCX at 0x8980E. Part+B0 is passed in R8 alongside part+F0 points in RDX and part+2A0 pose output in RCX to native tetra-to-mesh affine builder 0x7ECD0 at 0x89997. The independently inspected builder iterates four coefficient rows at a 0x10-byte stride and reads four floats from each row, establishing the full 64-byte coefficient span.
fields.name: bodyPart::poseCoefficients

fields.provenance: R12 is incoming attached body part, established by the actor assignment at part+580. Native affine transforms first write four successive 12-byte point addresses at +F0/+FC/+108/+114. LEA R12+F0 supplies RSI; ECX=6 at 0x155D82 and REP MOVSQ at 0x155D87 copy all 48 bytes into that same part's +120 history.
fields.name: bodyPart::points

fields.provenance: R12 is the attached body part. LEA part+120 supplies RDI for the six-qword copy from part+F0 at 0x155D87. At 0x155D92 the same part+120 is then the source of another six-qword copy into part+150. PartSettle independently copies six qwords from body+120 back to body+F0 at 0x89928-0x8993B.
fields.name: bodyPart::history

fields.provenance: R12 is the attached body part. LEA part+150 supplies RDI; part+120 supplies RSI at 0x155D92. ECX=6 at 0x155D9A and REP MOVSQ at 0x155D9F establish an exact 48-byte destination span, after the immediately preceding points-to-history copy.
fields.name: bodyPart::history2

fields.provenance: RBX remains the incoming part from RCX at 0x8980E. Part+2A0 is RCX (output), with part+F0 points in RDX and part+B0 coefficients in R8, at the call to 0x7ECD0. The independently inspected builder writes four rows at a 0xC-byte stride, each with three float components: exactly 48 bytes. Native affinePoint at 0x18870 reads basis triples at float indices 0..8 and translation at indices 9..11, confirming the twelve-float pose layout.
fields.name: bodyPart::pose

fields.provenance: The native hinge handler obtains the held scene node from drag manager+10, then loads node+160 into RAX at 0x11BC9B. That pointer is its physical body, also used for the +5C8 active-hinge byte. Its +420 pointer is passed to physical activation routine 0x7E3A0. This proves the pointer offset and body ownership; a self-root invariant is not proved by this call alone.
fields.name: bodyPart::rootPart

fields.provenance: R12 is loaded from actor+918 part-pointer array. For non-root part indices, this load reads part+428, then passes parent+520 to affine composition at 0x176BC3 with the current part's local pose and output part+520. Equivalent parent+550 and parent+2A0 uses occur later.
fields.name: bodyPart::parentPart

fields.provenance: R12 preserves incoming RDX (physical item part), RAX copies R12 at 0x155C39, and RBX is the incoming actor. This instruction explicitly writes actor to part+580, paired with storing the part into actor+C00 and actor+E88 indexed held-item slots. It is stronger owner evidence than the poseBuilder comparison of part+428 against part+580.
fields.name: bodyPart::character

fields.provenance: R12 is the current actor part from the +918 array. This branch is gated by the 32-bit part+C flag 0x4000 at 0x176BDF-0x176BE9. Part+5EC supplies RDX to native quaternion multiply 0x1CBD0 at 0x176BFD, combining with the part's native quaternion before conversion to affine rotation. The independently inspected multiply reads all four float components of its second operand, including param_2[3] in the scalar product, establishing the full 16-byte quaternion span.
fields.name: bodyPart::extraRotation

fields.provenance: R12 is still the actor's indexed physical part in the same outer loop. COMISS reads part+77C at 0x1775E9; the taken clamp branch reloads the same 32-bit float into XMM13 at 0x1775F6 before comparison/update of part+778. This is a per-part cap; the native code here does not make it exclusive to the head.
fields.name: bodyPart::slackCap

fields.provenance: RAX comes from the game viewport global then viewport+1C0. LEA camera+40 supplies RSI for REP MOVSQ with ECX=6, copying the camera's 48-byte pose.
fields.name: camera::pose

fields.provenance: RBX is the navigation controller argument; RAX=*(RBX+190), the same camera whose FOV and dirty field navSampler writes. Camera+70 is passed to native angle-to-orientation builder 0x1CD60. This proves the offset; matrix extent is not established by this call alone.
fields.name: camera::pose2

fields.provenance: RBX is native sampler; RAX=*(RBX+190), the camera used for pose and FOV output. The sampler writes integer 1 at camera+E4 when a sampled pose changes.
fields.name: camera::dirty

fields.provenance: RBX is T3DView argument, RSI=*(RBX+50) is its camera. MOVSS from camera+1C8 feeds angle conversion and tangent/projection scale calculations.
fields.name: camera::fov

fields.provenance: RSI is camera loaded from T3DView+50 at 0x9F2F7. MOVSS camera+1CC feeds near-plane projection arithmetic; 0x9F382 separately forwards it to the projection builder.
fields.name: camera::nearPlane

fields.provenance: Native controller initializer resolves viewport argument+1A8 view, then view+50 camera at 0x91E0B. Camera is stored into controller+190 and controller RBX is stored into camera+160, explicitly establishing the bidirectional relation used by navSampler.
fields.name: camera::controller

fields.provenance: RSI=*(sampler RBX+190), the camera. Native commit passes camera+40 as source and camera+A0 as destination to EXP_expand_affine_to_mat4 (0x1CEB0). This is expanded camera pose, distinct from view+A0 projection.
fields.name: camera::inverse

fields.provenance: RAX reloads the original viewport argument from stack+A8. Viewport+1A8 yields the view whose +1C4 mask controls the native ray query.
fields.name: viewport::view

fields.provenance: RAX first loads the named game viewport global at 0x11EB52; +1C0 yields the camera whose pose is copied immediately at +40.
fields.name: viewport::pickCamera

fields.provenance: RDX reloads original viewport argument from stack+A8. Viewport+1F0 yields manager; native code uses its +3C4/+3C8 sector count/list and then walks each sector's meshes.
fields.name: viewport::sceneManager

fields.provenance: RAX reloads original viewport argument from stack+B0. RDX=*(RAX+1F0) is its scene manager, also used below for sector +3C4/+3C8 traversal. Dword manager+C bit 0x2000000 gates the level-grid ray tests.
fields.name: sceneManager::flags

fields.provenance: RDX is scene manager obtained directly from original viewport+1F0 at 0x2463C7. Manager+320 supplies the grid context for native 0x1430F0 and 0x1431C0 level ray functions after manager+C bit 0x2000000 is tested.
fields.name: sceneManager::levelGrid

fields.provenance: RBX copies RCX (T3DView argument) at 0x9F2F4; view+50 yields camera and is followed immediately by FOV and near-plane reads.
fields.name: view::camera

fields.provenance: RBX is the incoming physical part (RCX) at 0x8B6F4. The native sample offset remains in XMM1 for sample-phase routine 0x8B7A0. After interpolating history2/history, MOV RAX,[RBX+18] at 0x8B75D resolves this part's mesh. LEA RCX,[RAX+A0] supplies output to 0x8B640 with the stack tetrahedron and part+B0 coefficients. The independently read 0x8B640 writes four rows at 0x10 stride, each with three floats; the last xyz write ends at byte 60. Row fourth components are not written or read by the camera adapter. The live controlled head's vtable+140 was verified as 0x8B6E0; nav checks that entry against this resolved named target before calling it.
fields.name: sceneNode::renderTransform

fields.provenance: RBX is mesh node obtained from current sector+1D0 indexed array at 0x8F985-0x8F98F. Mesh+40 supplies the matrix to world-to-local ray transformation, distinct from the earlier camera+40 transform.
fields.name: sceneNode::transform

fields.provenance: RBX preserves the incoming held scene node. Native 118920 normalizes and copies exactly 36 orientation bytes to node+70 at 118BC9-118BDA, preserving translation. It then resolves node+160 as the body and, under body+C bit 10000000, copies six qwords from node+70 to body+2A0 at 118BFD-118C0D. Native 50EB0 composes this node-local affine with parent+40 before updating node+40 and its children. The full 48-byte local affine and its parent-relative ownership are therefore witnessed independently of the separate sceneNode::transform field.
fields.name: sceneNode::localTransform

fields.provenance: RSI is physical part from drag manager+10 mesh then mesh+160. 0x11BE37 reloads part+18 mesh scene node; LEA mesh+64 supplies its position for a three-component subtraction. Replaces unsupported body-part offset +2C4 in tpHideKeep.
fields.name: sceneNode::transformOrigin

fields.provenance: RBX is mesh node from sector+1D0 indexed array, not sector itself. Its +E0 mask is ANDed with view query mask before the mesh ray test.
fields.name: sceneNode::passMask

fields.provenance: RAX reloads original scene-node argument from RBP-8. This routine composes node+70 with parent+128 transform+40, writes node+40, then reads signed last-child index+118; -1 is empty and loop index starts -1, increments before each recursive child call.
fields.name: sceneNode::lastChild

fields.provenance: RAX reloads original scene-node argument from RBP-8. Node+120 is dereferenced as an array of eight-byte child pointers at 0x50FC3; each pointer is passed recursively to the same native transform-propagation function at 0x50FC7.
fields.name: sceneNode::children

fields.provenance: RBX is behavior; 0xAC3DB loads behavior+28 character and 0xAC3DF loads character+18 mesh node. LEA mesh+140 is passed to string constructor 0x8C10 with length 15, then included in the native Character position overflow error. Repeats at 0xAC4BF; generic node child/parent names are also prepared at 0x50FEE/0x51058.
fields.name: sceneNode::name

fields.provenance: RSI is held object's body part loaded via drag manager+10 scene node then +160. RSI+18 yields that part's mesh node; mesh+128 yields its parent, whose +40 transform rotates the hinge calculation.
fields.name: sceneNode::parent

fields.provenance: RBX is player behaviour; RSI=*(RBX+28) is character at 0xBFA7D; RAX=*(RSI+18) is mesh scene node. Node+130 yields sector and its +64 origin is subtracted from aim coordinates.
fields.name: sceneNode::sector

fields.provenance: RBX copies drag-manager RCX. Manager+10 yields held scene node, then node+160 yields physical body part. Native release copies manager target points into body+F0.
fields.name: sceneNode::bodyPart

fields.provenance: RBX is mesh from sector+1D0 list. Native ray query calls mesh+3B0 with mesh+3B8 context after transforming ray by mesh+40.
fields.name: sceneNode::rayRoutine

fields.provenance: RBX is mesh from sector+1D0 list; mesh+3B8 becomes RCX for the immediately following indirect rayRoutine call at mesh+3B0.
fields.name: sceneNode::rayContext

fields.provenance: RDI is sector drawn from manager+3C8 sector array at 0x8F913-0x8F91D. Sector+64 supplies the three-component subtraction converting the global ray origin to sector-local coordinates.
fields.name: sector::origin

fields.provenance: RDI is current sector, traced from manager+3C8 list. Signed integer at +1C8 is compared against zero, then loop index starting -1 advances while index < lastMesh.
fields.name: sector::lastMesh

fields.provenance: RDI is current sector, +1D0 is dereferenced and indexed by sign-extended mesh index times eight; entries are scene-node pointers used for masks and ray tests.
fields.name: sector::meshes

fields.provenance: RDX reloads original fourth argument (output pick buffer) from stack+A0. Stores transformed ray origin at output+20 (8 bytes) and output+28 (4 bytes at 0x8F89B).
fields.name: pick::origin

fields.provenance: RDX is original output pick buffer from stack+A0. Stores normalized transformed ray direction at output+14 (8 bytes), followed by output+1C (4 bytes at 0x8F8BB).
fields.name: pick::direction

fields.provenance: RAX reloads output pick buffer from stack+A0. Scalar closest-hit/fallback distance is stored at output+2C before hit point computation at output+8.
fields.name: pick::distance

fields.provenance: RBX copies drag-manager RCX at entry. After completing release and clearing held-object pointer, native drop clears manager+8 as a 32-bit flags field.
fields.name: drag::flags

fields.provenance: RBX is the native drag manager. Ordinary LMB release branches on manager+14D: zero queues the held target points through 117000; nonzero takes invalid-placement recovery through 119CB0.
fields.name: drag::invalidDrop

fields.provenance: RCX is the native 0x38-byte release task from 117000. It is copied through RBX to RSI; the first QWORD is loaded as the physics body into R12 before release/reset work. The allocation is freed at 116FE8.
fields.name: heldRelease::body

fields.provenance: RSI copies the GUI-manager RCX. Consecutive X/Y DWORDs at +18/+1C are sent to hit testing. Mouse poll 2F7E0 writes this same pair after cursorPosition and returns early when it is unchanged.
fields.name: gui::pointerX

fields.provenance: Native double-click classification compares current +18/+1C against press +20/+24, requiring each difference below two pixels. A new accepted press copies current into that press pair at 300C5/300CC.
fields.name: gui::pressX

fields.provenance: RSI is the GUI manager. The QWORD at +30 is the hovered widget passed by 2FCC0 to its mouse dispatcher; live main-viewport identity was checked separately from these archive bytes.
fields.name: gui::hoverView

fields.provenance: Native press reads manager+40 and masks the low three physical mouse buttons; 2F7E0 also stores drag-threshold bit 100 in this DWORD. Native release 30240 clears it after dispatch.
fields.name: gui::buttons

fields.provenance: RBX copies drag-manager RCX at 0x119C38. Manager+10 is tested and loaded, then +160 yields held node's body part; manager+10 is cleared at 0x119C82 after release.
fields.name: drag::object

fields.provenance: RSI receives drag manager+40; RDI receives manager+10 scene node -> +160 body -> +F0 points. REP MOVSQ with ECX=6 copies exactly 48 bytes during cancellation at 119C30. Native 11A690 initializes this span from the original grabbed body's points; normal 11F610 placement updates body+F0 and the separate last-valid span at drag+88. The retained targetPoints identifier therefore denotes the original recovery snapshot, not live placement geometry.
fields.name: drag::targetPoints
